note: Mapping from internal doc 16-tool standardized decomposition (docs 01-05) to the public web 14-tool canonical set. The web treats the 14-tool form as the public-facing canonical structure; the doc's 16-tool form is the internal expanded decomposition useful for fine-grained attribution.

T01.collapse_reason: Both target the upstream content-validity layer: T01 clarifies what is being claimed (T1) and links it to the protected interest / harm pathway (T4).

T03.collapse_reason: T5 + T8 are usually co-applied (scenarios need information-flow framing, esp. for privacy). T5a/T5b and the information-flow schema are preserved as subsections within T03.

T04.collapse_reason: 1-1; web renames Risk-tier → Risk-Tier & Hazard Taxonomy.

T05.collapse_reason: 1-1; web emphasises Cross-Lingual to make the language axis explicit.

T06.collapse_reason: 1-1; T9a/T9b/T9c are preserved as internal subtypes.

T07.collapse_reason: Web-only construct: Behavioural Coverage Matrix. Not in doc's 16. Spans CheckList-style behavioural testing + the coverage view that the doc folds into T5/T9. Retained for cases where coverage is the primary deliverable rather than the means.

T10.collapse_reason: 1-1; web adds Claim Verification Pipeline framing for trustworthiness/factuality benches.

T12.collapse_reason: Web folds the three label/scoring/judge tools into one Rubric-Based & Multi-Judge Evaluation Protocol because in practice label structure + scoring rubric + judge calibration ship as one evaluation package; the doc preserves the finer split for internal source-attribution.

T13.collapse_reason: Doc's T16 governance package is split in the web into two: T13 (Reproducible Evaluation & Benchmark Card Package) takes T16a + T16c.

T14.collapse_reason: T14 (Lifecycle, Hidden-Split & Contamination Governance) takes T16b + T16d from doc T16.
